clue.text: 27 fought to replace university with hospital management when Hitler disposed of his storm troopers

definitions.text: when Hitler disposed of his storm troopers

indicators.note: management here is handling or manipulating, so the combined letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: 27 refers to the answer at 27 across, the former London mayor

indicators.note: to replace X with Y signals swapping one letter of the word for another
with names the incoming letter in the swap

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A former London mayor is pictured scrapping with management, set against a dark episode of Nazi history.
explanation.walkthrough: FOUGHT with its U swapped for H gives FOHGHT; add KENLIVINGSTONE and 'management' rearranges the twenty letters. The 1934 purge of the SA brownshirts is known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the historical name for the 1934 purge in which Hitler had leaders of the SA brownshirts killed.

clue.text: The end for Brighton? Paul's reminded about "If at first you don't succeed …"

indicators.note: the end for a word is its final letter, here taken from the town's name
about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter, Paul, muses on a seaside town's demise and an old proverb about perseverance.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of Brighton, N, then 'about' rearranges PAULSREMINDED (the S of Paul's counts) into ILDESPERANDUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto means never despair, the same encouragement as the proverb urging you to try, try again.

clue.text: Messenger girl accepts fare from France

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one word holds another inside it

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
brie is a French cheese, food from France

explanation.surface: A delivery girl is handed some French food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is the archangel who acts as God's messenger in the Bible.

clue.text: Cardinal following short, narrow passage emitted tremulous noises

indicators.note: following puts the colour after the shortened passage
short means the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: a twitten is a Sussex dialect word for a narrow alley between buildings
cardinal is a deep scarlet colour, as in a cardinal's robes

explanation.surface: A cardinal walking behind someone down a cramped alley makes quavering sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The narrow passage is a southern English dialect word for an alley, little known outside Sussex; 'short' trims its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Twittered means made a series of light, trembling chirps, like birdsong.

clue.text: Formidable weapon thus gripped in charge

indicators.note: in places the gripping combination inside the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: gripped means held within, so one word sits inside another

parts.note: arm is a word for a weapon, as in firearm
so means thus, in that way

explanation.surface: A weapon held by someone in charge sounds formidable.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'gripped' works first inside the weapon, then 'in' puts the result inside the charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome and formidable are synonyms describing something frightening in its power.

clue.text: Musical books contained bunkum

indicators.note: contained means held inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A musical's scripts were full of nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air means empty talk or nonsense, the same as bunkum.

clue.text: Some modern Italian? On the contrary

definitions.text: Some modern Italian? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary means the other way round, so the run of letters is read backwards
some means a part of the words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a language is a form of modern Italian and is told the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading NITAL backwards gives the answer; the clue as a whole also defines it, since Latin is old Italian, the contrary of modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the ancient language of Italy, the opposite of modern Italian, from which Italian descends.

clue.text: Writer finds an example of his work half-hearted during month

indicators.note: during means within a time span, so the pieces sit inside the month

parts.note: Nov is the abbreviation for November
an gives the article a

indicators.note: half-hearted means losing half of the word's centre, one of its two middle letters

parts.note: an author's work is a book

explanation.surface: A novelist's latest book is found lacking spirit sometime this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes half of the doubled middle letter pair of the word for his work, not half of the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was a Russian-American novelist, author of Lolita and Pale Fire.

clue.text: Relation's writing

definitions.meaning: a relation means a connection or matching between things
writing here means letters exchanged between people

explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence means both agreement between things and an exchange of letters.

clue.text: Student can rub it out; you can rub it in

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A contrast between rubbing something out and rubbing something in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rub it out' tempts as a whole idiom; 'out' alone is the anagram signal working on CANRUBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lubricant such as oil or grease is applied by rubbing it into a surface.

clue.text: Expression of appreciation then otherwise anathema

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
otherwise here means the opposite kind of expression, a jeer of disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone says thanks and then the opposite, something forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks; the contrary expression is BOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden and abhorred, as an anathema is.

clue.text: Endlessly overworked writer

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are read backwards
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: toiled means worked hard

explanation.surface: A writer who is perpetually overworked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overworked' splits as 'over' plus 'worked': TOILED loses its end to give TOILE, and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot and T. S. Eliot were both writers of the first rank.

clue.text: Where wind gathered, Alastair Campbell a king you have to admit

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Alastair Campbell, Tony Blair's press chief, was a famous spin doctor or spinner
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A remark that Blair's press chief must let a king in.
explanation.walkthrough: Campbell was the press secretary to British prime minister Tony Blair, a byword for political spin; SPINNER takes in A K.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinnaker is a large sail at a yacht's bow that billows out to catch the wind.

clue.text: Religious devotees forbidding lager to be passed round

indicators.note: passed round means put around something, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Pils is short for Pilsner, a type of lager
grim means stern or forbidding

explanation.surface: Pious people disapprove of lager going round.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilgrims are religious believers who journey to a holy place.

clue.text: See 1
Infamous rejection of South American city by America

parts.note: no to expresses refusal of something
Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil
US stands for United States, America

explanation.surface: America turns down a Brazilian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, the same as infamous.

clue.text: No title given to magazine that's turned camp

indicators.note: turned means the whole run is reversed

parts.note: taken as written
Sir is a title for a knight
rag is slang for a cheap newspaper or magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine refuses to award a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a body of troops stationed at a fort or camp, and the place itself.

clue.text: Country where fish filmed following river

indicators.note: following puts the fish's name after the river's letter

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps
A Fish Called Wanda is a 1988 comedy film

explanation.surface: A country where a fish was filmed beyond a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a landlocked country in east-central Africa.

clue.text: On the continent, local time holds unfinished puzzle up

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read upwards, backwards
unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rebus is a picture puzzle

explanation.surface: A European puzzle-setter at the local takes time over a half-done puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the neighbourhood pub, so the definition asks for a continental pub or inn; 'up' reverses the shortened puzzle in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An auberge is a French inn, the continental counterpart of a British local pub.

clue.text: Performers tell nothing to deprived performer

parts.note: the cast is the set of performers in a show
to rat is to tell on someone, inform
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Actors refuse to tell anything to a disadvantaged colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrato was a male singer castrated before puberty, deprived to keep a high voice.

clue.text: Style of trade adapted for business

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A trade style adapted for business.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is a decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Writer removes them in casual conversation?

definitions.text: Writer removes them in casual conversation?

parts.words: Writer removes them in casual conversation?
parts.note: the writer's surname, said slackly, resembles someone saying a person 'has 'im off', dropped aitches and all, meaning takes him off

explanation.walkthrough: The joke rests on lazy speech: dropped H sounds and a slurred 'off' turn a phrase about taking someone off into the science-fiction writer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific American science-fiction writer, author of I, Robot.

clue.text: Sprayer of plant's fluid about to cover blue ground

indicators.note: to cover means to enclose, so one piece goes around another
about means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: resin is the sticky fluid secreted by plants such as pines

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A device for spraying sap over crushed blue material.
explanation.walkthrough: RESIN turned 'about' gives NISER, which covers EBUL, the letters of BLUE 'ground'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebuliser turns liquid medicine into a fine spray or mist for inhaling.

clue.text: Proper support, two thirds of 100%

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair

indicators.note: two thirds of a three-letter word drops one of its letters

parts.note: 100% means all of it

explanation.surface: A recommended amount of support.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal means permitted by law, proper in the official sense.

clue.text: Highly praised, or not?

definitions.meaning: the opposite sense, scolded, since to rate someone is an old word for berating them

explanation.definitionFit: Rated means esteemed, but the old verb rate means to scold angrily, its opposite.

clue.text: Bend on ring bent to detach ropes

parts.note: a U-bend, a pipe shaped like the letter

indicators.note: bent means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bend in a ring bent out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig a ship is to strip it of its rigging, its ropes.

clue.text: Carelessly manage novice in terribly moving service

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are thrown into disorder
novice read as no vice means the word loses those four letters

explanation.surface: A beginner is in a dreadfully emotional church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novice' reads as 'no vice', leaving SER from SERVICE; with MOVING, 'terribly' rearranges the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To misgovern is to rule or manage badly.

clue.text: Reformed Leninist evoking one lost capitalist leader?

indicators.note: reformed means re-formed, rearranged into a new order
lost signals that one letter goes missing from the pool

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A reformed Leninist sounds off about a fallen capitalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LENINIST EVOKING less I are rearranged. The definition is a pun: 'capital-ist leader', leader of the capital, London.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the first elected Mayor of London, so the leader of the capital, which gives the pun.
